solutions.check: 30 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 29 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Fat French customers are very jumpy

definitions.note: adjective phrase standing for the insects noted for leaping

parts.note: gras is the French word for fat
shoppers are customers in a shop

explanation.surface: Overweight Parisian shoppers are on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects leap great distances on powerful hind legs, so they are the very type of jumping creature.

clue.text: They are glad when the ball is over

definitions.text: They are glad when the ball is over

parts.words: They are glad when the ball is over
parts.note: not partygoers at the end of a dance but players relieved when a shot passes over the crossbar

explanation.surface: Weary dancers relieved when the party ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepers guarding the net are pleased when a shot sails over the bar.

clue.text: Cave in a pleasant resort

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A grotto at a nice holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for a cavern, used by Shakespeare in Othello.

clue.text: Making a neat splash, going by tube

definitions.text: Making a neat splash, going by tube

parts.words: Making a neat splash, going by tube
parts.note: a soda siphon adds a splash to neat spirits; drawing liquid through a pipe

explanation.surface: Cutting a fine figure while travelling on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going by tube' suggests the London Underground; it means liquid moving through a pipe, as from a soda siphon into a neat whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing liquid through a bent pipe by pressure, as a soda siphon squirts into a drink.

clue.text: M.A. here with old plough-boy's goal?

definitions.text: M.A. here with old plough-boy's goal?

parts.words: M.A. here with old plough-boy's goal?
parts.note: the Latin tag written after an Oxford master's degree, read as a ploughman's cry urging his beast forward

explanation.surface: A graduate follows the aim of a ploughman of old.
explanation.walkthrough: Graduates write M.A. Oxon for an Oxford master's degree; split as OX ON, it is a ploughboy driving his beast forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for the Latin Oxoniensis, marking an Oxford degree.

clue.text: Dose Bert's head for these jerks

definitions.note: the kind of jerks meant, physical jerks or exercises; adjective sense

parts.note: physic is an old word for medicine, a dose
Bert is short for Albert, which begins AL

explanation.surface: Give Bert a spoonful of medicine to cure these fools.
explanation.walkthrough: Physical jerks are old British slang for keep-fit exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical jerks are gymnastic exercises, so the word describes these jerks.

clue.text: Acres or Beverley

definitions.meaning: Bob Acres, a suitor in Sheridan's The ...
Ensign Beverley, the disguise of Captain Absolute in the same play

explanation.surface: Land measures or a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Both men compete for Lydia Languish in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals, so each is a competitor for her hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Each character is a competitor for the same woman's affections.

clue.text: To Blanch, so crippling a toil in summertime abroad

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the French word

parts.note: ete is French for summer

indicators.note: crippling suggests the letters are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: Bleaching after hard work under a foreign summer sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' tells the solver the summer word is French; 'crippling' works on A TOIL alone, and 'in' sets the result within the summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To etiolate a plant is to make it pale by keeping it from light, as a gardener blanches celery.

clue.text: Bald prophet

parts.note: the biblical seer mocked by youths as baldhead

explanation.surface: A hairless seer.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2 Kings 2, boys jeer 'Go up, thou bald head' at Elijah's successor, and bears maul them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament prophet who succeeded Elijah and was mocked for his baldness.

clue.text: Opposed to sham in the choir

definitions.note: a phrase pointing to what happens in a choir, standing for the noun

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to
phony means fake, a sham

explanation.surface: Someone objects to fakery among the singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Responsive singing, with two halves of a choir answering each other, is the musical practice meant.

clue.text: It's necessary to be quick

definitions.meaning: in the old sense of alive, as in the quick and the dead

explanation.surface: Speed is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential things are vital; and vital also means living, the old meaning of quick.

clue.text: General's wrath was grave

parts.note: a Parliamentary general of the Civil War whose corpse royalist anger dug from its tomb and hanged after the Restoration

explanation.surface: A commander's anger was serious.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Ireton, Cromwell's son-in-law and general, died in 1651; in 1661 his body was exhumed and hanged at Tyburn, so the wrath reached him in the grave. IRE (wrath) also opens the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireton was a general in the New Model Army whose remains suffered posthumous punishment.

clue.text: Philosopher with one bad sun peopling the earth

definitions.note: describes the vast numbers of humans, standing for the noun

parts.note: John Stuart Mill, the English philosopher
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: bad signals the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: the setter meant son, whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thinker and a wayward offspring among Earth's teeming population.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram must make ONS, which SUN cannot give: the setter or compositor wrote sun for son. 'bad' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's population is counted in vast numbers, thousands of thousands of people.

clue.text: Hanoverian namesake of Traddles's "dearest girl in the world"

definitions.text: Hanoverian namesake of Traddles's "dearest girl in the world"

parts.words: Hanoverian namesake of Traddles's "dearest girl in the world"
parts.note: the Electress of Hanover, mother of George I, shares a name with Tommy Traddles's beloved Sophy in David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A Hanoverian royal shares her name with a Dickens character's sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: In David Copperfield, Traddles calls Sophy, a curate's daughter, 'the dearest girl in the world'. Sophia of Hanover was the electress through whom the Hanoverians came to the British throne.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophy is a pet form of the name borne by the Electress of Hanover.

clue.text: Tell churchwarden to take a pew and shut up?

definitions.text: Tell churchwarden to take a pew and shut up?

parts.words: Tell churchwarden to take a pew and shut up?
parts.note: a churchwarden is also a long clay tobacco pipe; telling it to sit gives a phrase meaning be quiet

explanation.surface: Asking a parish official to sit and be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: A churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay pipe as well as a parish officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an order to stop talking, literally a pipe told to sit.

clue.text: French spouse beat a gipsy love ? Ask Wallace

definitions.note: the gipsy heroine and beloved of William Vincent Wallace's 1845 opera

parts.note: mari is French for husband
to tan is to thrash or beat

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's husband thrashes his gipsy sweetheart; consult Wallace about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ask Wallace' points to the composer William Vincent Wallace, whose opera of this name concerns a Spanish gipsy singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The opera's title character is a street singer of gipsy blood whom the hero loves.

clue.text: Bury a liar right away, additional matters being involved

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for among other things

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: right away says R, the abbreviation for right, is removed

explanation.surface: Get rid of a liar quickly, with other business mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' removes R from A LIAR, leaving ALIA. The Latin phrase means among other things.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means among other things, used when further matters come into it.

clue.text: Market garden produce, say, on the border?

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: to market garden produce is to sell veg

explanation.surface: Vegetables grown at the edge of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Market' is a verb: sell veg, spoken, matches the word for a fabric edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The self-finished edge of woven cloth that stops it fraying.

clue.text: I'm a dog, by name donkey-ish: that's called in question

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
a pug is a small breed of dog
Ned, as in Neddy, is a stock name for a donkey

explanation.surface: A dog introduces itself as having a donkey's name, which is disputed.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim is to challenge or dispute its truth, so impugned means doubted openly.

clue.text: Existential estate unreachable on foot

definitions.note: describes a place cut off by water, standing for the noun

parts.note: existential relates to being, and is is the verb of existence
land, as in landed estate

explanation.surface: A philosophical property you cannot walk to.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of ground surrounded by water cannot be walked to.

clue.text: What a tiller does with livestock

definitions.meaning: a tiller is a boat's helm lever, which guides the craft
young castrated oxen raised for beef

explanation.surface: A farmer's tiller and his cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiller' suggests a farmer tilling the soil beside his livestock, but here it is the bar on a boat's rudder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller directs a boat's course; bullocks raised for beef also go by this name.

clue.text: Musical limitations

parts.note: conditions attached as limits, and the violin section of an orchestra

explanation.surface: The restrictions of a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no strings attached' means without conditions; the orchestra's bowed section shares the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions attached restrict a deal; the violins, violas and cellos are the musical sense.

clue.text: Youthful idyll of old man

definitions.meaning: a country name for southernwood, an aromatic shrub

explanation.surface: An elderly man recalls a romance of his youth.
explanation.walkthrough: Southernwood (Artemisia abrotanum) is called both old man and lad's love in English country speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A young fellow's sweetheart affair, and also the shrub southernwood, whose other folk name is old man.

clue.text: Time for some Schubert

parts.note: the operetta ... Time is built on Schubert's melodies

explanation.surface: The moment to play a little Schubert.
explanation.walkthrough: Lilac Time (1922) is an operetta arranged from Schubert's music, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The flowering shrub names the Schubert pastiche operetta Lilac Time.

clue.text: Decorous in natural colouring

definitions.meaning: the heraldic term for a charge shown in its true colours

explanation.surface: Something seemly in its native hues.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry, a lion or tree described this way is shown in its natural colours rather than a tincture.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly conduct is correct; heraldry uses the same word for charges shown in their real colours.

clue.text: Piano gives wild hoot, then snap!

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: wild signals the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A pianist gives a wild hoot and then snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges HOOT into HOTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a casual snapshot, a quick picture.

clue.text: In dusky girl's embrace I grow familiar

definitions.note: the girl's name grows into its familiar pet form

indicators.note: embrace shows the girl's name holds the letter within it

parts.note: Eve, a girl's name that also means evening, the dusky hour

explanation.surface: Held by a dark-haired girl, I become intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminutive pet name made from Eve, the friendly familiar version of it.

clue.text: Could be a top-flight post

parts.note: read not as a first-rate job but as an upright at the head of a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: Perhaps an elite appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright pillar at the top or bottom of a staircase, supporting the handrail.

clue.text: Was Faust in the 88th Foot?

parts.note: Faust sold his soul to Mephistopheles, and the 88th Regiment of Foot carried a fiendish nickname

explanation.surface: Did Goethe's scholar serve in a British infantry regiment?
explanation.walkthrough: The 88th Foot, the Connaught Rangers, were nicknamed the Devil's Own; Faust, having sold his soul, belonged to the devil too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the soul-selling doctor and the Connaught Rangers regiment were said to belong to Satan.

clue.text: Car components for the Red Queen

definitions.text: Car components for the Red Queen

parts.words: Car components for the Red Queen
parts.note: pedals that speed a car up, suited to the Looking-Glass monarch who cries Faster! Faster!

explanation.surface: Motor parts for a chess piece.
explanation.walkthrough: In Through the Looking-Glass the Red Queen drags Alice along shouting 'Faster! Faster!', running just to stay in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedals that make a car go faster, exactly what the hurrying Red Queen would want.
